newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, May 7 - After a vigorous month-on-month increase of 35.7 percent in March, the seasonal rise in palm production slowed down in April. CPO production increased around six percent or 40,000 tonnes to an estimated 723,000 tonnes. On an annual basis, production posted a strong growth of about 17 percent which was much better than the 7.8 percent recorded in January-March. However, our field crop surveys indicated growth in the second quarter is likely to be little changed from that posted in the first quarter.

In other words, we expect a deceleration in the pace of growth to around four percent in May-June. Also, for the second-half of this year, we project growth to be not more than three percent. For the whole year, CPO production is projected to increase five percent to 8.8 million tonnes. With cash CPO price in January-June expected to average around 1,310 ringgit, or seven percent more than the same period last year, it is quite likely some replanting of old palms could be delayed 6-12 months from the original replanting schedule. In our recent field trips we saw palms planted in 1968-71 still under harvest.

An estimated 50,000 hectares per annum are due for replanting in 1997-1998. CPO output was hardly sufficient to keep pace with continuing good demand. We estimate stocks at end April were further drawn down by some 10,000 tonnes to around 350,000 tonnes. In contrast, stocks of PPO were estimated to have increased by 15,000 tonnes to around 345,000 tonnes to meet larger than normal export shipments schedule in the first week of May.

Total palm oil stocks at end-April thus amounted to an estimated 695,000 tonnes or hardly changed from our previous estimate of around 700,000 tonnes and the month ago level of 689,600 tonnes. Exports of palm oil are estimated to have risen to 610,000 tonnes in April from preliminary exports of 565,200 tonnes in March reported by PORLA. The increase in exports was wholly accounted by India and Pakistan which collectively raised their offtake by some 75,000 tonnes to an estimated 185,000 tonnes. Exports to China remained good at around 115,000 tonnes.

These three major importers are likely to continue to account for one-half of Malaysian palm oil exports for another month or two. Strong palm oil fundamentals provided the impetus for continued strength in price in both the cash and futures markets. For the week ended May 2, CPO futures gained 38-20 ringgit. This marked the fourth consecutive week of advance and brought the cumulative gains over four weeks to 83-54 ringgit. The spot May futures contract gained the most. A slowdown in covering activities coupled with profit-taking resulted in price pulling back 30-17 ringgit in the last two days.

May settled at 1,304 ringgit yesterday after posting an intraday high of 1,342 ringgit a day earlier. Cash CPO averaged 1,355.50 ringgit on May 5 while RBD olein for May shipment was traded as high as $607.50 on May 2 before easing to $602.50 yesterday.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).
